The Vice-Chancellor of the University of Uyo, Prof. Christopher Ekong, has hailed a Computer Engineering graduate, Abasifreke Nkanang, who finished with a cumulative grade point average of 4.91 as the overall best graduating student at its 31st and 32nd combined convocation. Ekong, speaking at the university’s convocation held on Thursday, described Nkanang’s performance as outstanding and a source of pride to the university. “Nkanang’s achievement is clear evidence of diligence, discipline and commitment to academic excellence,” he said. However, Nkanang attributed his emergence as the best graduate of the institution to goal-setting and focus. Speaking shortly after the convocation, Nkanang said setting a clear academic goal from his first year helped him attain the feat. If it is academics, aim for the high echelon of graduates,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The Head of Community Relations at Oriental Energy Resources Limited, Dr Uwem Ite, said the company was proud of Nkanang’s achievement and all the beneficiaries of its scholarship programme. “Oriental Energy is producing offshore in Akwa Ibom. As part of our corporate social responsibility, we have a scholarship scheme for university students in Akwa Ibom. “The overall best graduating student of this convocation was a beneficiary of that scholarship and he read engineering. Our financial support really enabled him to get to the point that he is now,” he stated. Emem Julius
